items.stem: An eval set of 500 clean prompts scores 96 percent. Production users paste long documents and send empty messages, and failures rise. The set must predict production at a low daily cost.
options: Add production samples with long, empty, and irrelevant inputs, and grade the checkable cases with code.
Have three reviewers grade every case by hand before each daily run, to catch subtle errors.
Enable the Console evaluation tool to build the production sample, then score the sample with code.
Add a versioned set with a dashboard per case type, plus production samples that include edge cases.
items.rationale: Production samples expose failures that clean prompts hide. Code graders score checkable cases at low cost, so the daily run stays cheap.
items.trap: A Console tool that builds the production sample sounds like a shortcut, but the docs describe no tool that samples production traffic.

items.stem: A nightly run grades 30,000 outputs. Most outputs need an exact match on one field, and a few need a judgment about tone. The team must avoid human graders, and each grader must be reliable.
options: Send all 30,000 outputs to an LLM grader without a reliability test, to keep the setup simple.
Add a second LLM grader that cross-checks each tone verdict before the run ends.
Grade exact-match outputs with code, and grade tone with an LLM grader after a reliability test.
Use a grader setting that caches each verdict, so repeated nightly runs skip the scoring step.
items.rationale: Code graders are the fastest and most reliable method for exact matches. An LLM grader handles tone only after a test confirms its reliability.
items.trap: A grader setting that caches verdicts sounds like a cost fix, but the docs do not describe such a setting.

items.stem: A team builds an eval set for a chat assistant. The set must match real traffic and cover unusual input. The team must not hand-grade every case. Which two steps meet these constraints?
options: Use a built-in Console sampler that labels ambiguous cases automatically.
Sample recent production traffic, so the cases match the real task mix.
Rebuild the set every hour from the live traffic log, so it never ages.
Add empty, long, and irrelevant inputs as edge cases, with expected answers that code can check.
items.rationale: Sampled production cases reflect the real task mix. Edge cases expose failures that clean samples hide, and code checks the expected answers.
items.trap: An hourly rebuild of the set looks thorough, but the constraints do not need that upkeep.
